WelcomeStep.description: You are going to participate in a user test that aims to evaluate the ease of use and understanding of a digital application. This type of test helps us detect possible technological barriers and improve the experience for everyone.
WelcomeStep.phases: Throughout the test, we will guide you through different phases. In each one, you will be clearly told what to do. There are no right or wrong answers: what interests us is how you interact with the system.
WelcomeStep.summary: Here you can see a summary of the phases you will follow:
WelcomeStep.ready: When you are ready, click the button to start. You can move at your own pace and stop at any time if you need to.

PreTasksStep.title: Tasks
PreTasksStep.heading: Let's begin the tasks phase
PreTasksStep.tasksSuffix: tasks related to using the tool. There are no correct or incorrect answers: what matters is how you interact.
PreTasksStep.instruction: When you are ready, click the button to begin.
PreTasksStep.recordingDescription: During the tasks, we may collect different types of data to understand your interaction with the system. Depending on the specific task, the following may be recorded:
PreTasksStep.recordingNote: You will be notified before any recording begins. All data is collected solely for research purposes and handled according to privacy guidelines.

CalibrationStep.title: Eye Tracking Calibration
CalibrationStep.heading: Before starting calibration
CalibrationStep.description: We are going to prepare your device to record your eye movement. This will allow us to understand how you navigate the screen during the test.
CalibrationStep.process: Calibration involves following points that will appear on the screen with your eyes. It is important that you are in a well-lit place, sit comfortably, and keep your head stable.
CalibrationStep.instruction: When you are ready, press the button to start calibration.

eyeTracking.title: Eye Tracking Calibration
eyeTracking.description1: We will provide your device to record your eye movements.
eyeTracking.description2: Follow the points that appear on the screen.

labels.noteText: The selected model will be used for the calibration process. The default model is Linear Regression. Some models may take longer to train than others. So please be patient.

tooltips.pointNumber: Number of calibration points shown on the screen (more points = higher accuracy).
tooltips.samplesPerPoint: How many gaze samples are collected per calibration point. Higher values improve precision but increase duration.
tooltips.msPerPoint: Duration (in milliseconds) to capture data per point. Defines how long the user must look at each target.
tooltips.threshold: Maximum distance (in pixels) allowed between calibration samples before they are discarded. Controls spatial tolerance.
tooltips.radius: Adjust the radius of the calibration point. Larger values make the point bigger.
tooltips.offset: Offset (in pixels) to adjust the calibration area position.

help.createtest: How do I create a test?
help.createtestanswer: To create a test, begin by clicking on the plus icon, selecting Heuristic Test. Then, specify the particulars of your project. Finally, proceed to the dedicated manager page.
help.heuristictest: How I setup my Heuristic test?
help.heuristictestanswer: To set up your Heuristic test, start by accessing the 'Edit Test' option. Then, click on the plus icon button to add a title and the question to your heuristic. Next, navigate to the options section to create the answer options and their respective values. Finally, save the modifications.
help.deletetestanswer: To delete your test, navigate to the left sidebar and click on the 'Settings' button. Then, select the 'DELETE TEST' button.
help.createtemplateanswer: To create a template for your test, navigate to the left sidebar and click on the 'Settings' button. Then, select the 'CREATE TEMPLATE' option.
help.usetemplateanswer: To utilize a template, navigate to the Tests page. Under the Create Templates section, you'll find your personal templates. Additionally, you can explore public templates.
help.previewtestanswer: On the leftside bar, click on the 'Preview' option then start the test answering the questions & finally clicking the bottom right button to save and submit the preview which can be later analysed in the 'Answers' section.
help.importcsvanswer: To import your CSV, navigate to the 'Edit Test' section, then click the 'UPDATE' button. Select your CSV file containing the heuristics.
help.invitecooperatorsanswer: To invite collaborators, navigate to the manager page of your test. From there, select 'Cooperators' on the left sidebar. Click on 'Select cooperator' and enter the email of your collaborator. Choose the collaborators role, then send the invitation by clicking on the bottom right button.
help.analyseresultsanswer: To analyze your results, navigate to the manager page of your test. From there, select 'Answers' on the left sidebar. Here, you can visualize statistics, evaluators, and heuristics.
help.sendmessage: How to send a message to my cooperators?
help.sendmessageanswer: To send a message, navigate to the manager page of your test. Select 'Cooperators' from the left sidebar. Click on the three dots icon next to the cooperator you want to message. Then, choose 'Send a message' and write your message with a title and content.

introduction.title: 1. Introduction
introduction.content: Ruxailab is an open-source project committed to protecting your privacy. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, and protect any information you provide when using the Project.

informationCollected.title: 2. Information We Collect
informationCollected.content: As an open-source project, we typically do not collect personal information directly. However, if you interact with our website or services (e.g., signing up for an account or submitting a contact form), we may collect:

items.email: Email addresses (e.g., for account creation or newsletters)
items.usage: Usage data (e.g., analytics on how the website is accessed)
items.contributions: Contributions (e.g., your GitHub username if you contribute to the Project)

usage.title: 3. How We Use Your Information
usage.content: We may use the information we collect to:

items.improve: Provide and improve the Project and its services
items.communicate: Communicate with you (e.g., respond to inquiries or notify you of updates)
items.analyze: Analyze usage to improve user experience

sharing.title: 4. Data Sharing
sharing.content: We do not sell or share your personal information with third parties, except as required by law or to protect the Project (e.g., in the case of abuse or fraud).

cookies.title: 5. Cookies
cookies.content: Our website may use cookies to enhance your experience (e.g., to remember your preferences). You can disable cookies in your browser settings, but this may affect the functionality of the website.

security.title: 6. Data Security
security.content: We take reasonable measures to protect any data we collect, but no method of transmission over the internet is 100% secure. We cannot guarantee the absolute security of your information.

rights.title: 7. Your Rights
rights.content: Depending on your location, you may have the right to access, correct, or delete any personal information we hold about you. Please contact us to exercise these rights.

changes.title: 8. Changes to This Policy
changes.content: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. We will notify users of significant changes by posting a notice on the Project's website or repository.

contact.title: 9. Contact Us
contact.content: If you have any questions about this Privacy Policy, please contact us.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
faq.subtitle: Find answers to common questions about Ruxailab.

q1.question: 1. What is Ruxailab?
q1.answer: Ruxailab is an open-source platform designed to collect usability feedback from users. It allows you to gather user reviews, analyze them, and create comprehensive reports to better understand your application's usability. Additionally, it offers heuristic tests, enabling experts to evaluate your application's compliance with usability principles. It is maintained by a community of contributors and licensed under the MIT License.

q2.question: 2. How do I get started with the Project?
q2.answer_part2: to download the source code. Check out the documentation for installation instructions and examples. You can also visit our

q3.question: 3. Can I contribute to the Project?
q3.answer: Absolutely! We welcome contributions from the community. Please read our contribution guidelines in the repository and submit a pull request with your changes.

q4.question: 4. What license does the Project use?
q4.answer: The Project is licensed under the MIT License. This means you can use, modify, and distribute the Project freely, as long as you include the license and copyright notice.

q5.question: 5. How do I report a bug or request a feature?
q5.answer: You can report bugs or request features by opening an issue on our
q5.answer_part2: . Please provide as much detail as possible to help us address your request.

q6.question: 6. Is there a community for Ruxailab?
q6.answer_part2: to connect with other users and contributors, ask questions, and share ideas.

q7.question: 7. How is my data handled?
q7.answer: We take your privacy seriously. Please see our
q7.answer_part2: for details on how we collect and use your information.

q8.question: 8. Who maintains the Project?
q8.answer: The Project is maintained by a team of volunteers and contributors. You can find more information about the maintainers in the Project's repository.

q9.question: 9. Still have questions?
q9.answer: If you have additional questions, please contact us.
